consensus_summary: The consensus identifies 'the truth' primarily as Jesus Christ himself (the personal self-revelation of God), with close extensions to God's word, the gospel, the Spirit of truth, sound doctrine, covenant faithfulness, and moral integrity; this is settled and layered around Johannine texts (esp. John 14:6), with alternatives treated as complementary emphases rather than rivals.
book_summary: The book identifies 'the truth' as God's law—the standard, while explicitly noting the common teaching as Christ Himself and God's word (the gospel that sets free).
consensus_core_identification: Jesus Christ as the personal embodiment of truth (with God's word/gospel as immediate extension)
boundary_disagreement: Consensus admits God's law (via Ps 119 and word-language) only as secondary/OT background or alternative while centering Christ; the book elevates law to the sole primary identification and demotes the Christological reading to a noted 'commonly taught' view.
material_contradiction: The book replaces the consensus primary referent (Christ himself) with God's law, so the two cores cannot both serve as the principal identification of 'the truth' in the same symbolic sense and context.
rationale: Minimum cores are non-equivalent: consensus unifies on the personal Christological identification (John 14:6 et al.) as primary, treating law/word as extension or alternative; the book instead cores exclusively on God's law and flags the Christ/gospel reading as the common alternative. This substitutes rather than narrows or broadens the central referent (even though law appears among consensus alternatives and the referents are related), producing divergence. Extensions partially overlap on law/word cases but the replaced primary drives the classification.
strongest_objection: The most direct and dominant NT identification—'I am the way, and the truth, and the life' (John 14:6) and related Johannine texts—is demoted by the book despite being the settled consensus center, while a single OT statement that 'thy law is the truth' is elevated.
